Assume small-deformation, linear-elastic, Euler-Bernoulli (plane sections remain plane) solid mechanics for a prismatic rectangular beam.
The cross-section is rectangular with width b = 50 mm and height h = 120 mm.
The second moment of area about the horizontal neutral axis is I_z = b·h³ / 12.
The internal bending moment at the section of interest is M = 4,000,000 N·mm, sagging, taken as positive under the convention that y is positive upward from the centroidal (neutral) axis.
The governing relation for the normal bending stress at an arbitrary fiber located at distance y from the neutral axis is σ_x = −(M · y) / I_z.
Evaluate σ_x at three specified fiber locations: the neutral axis (y = 0 mm), the top fiber (y = +60 mm, compression under sagging moment), and the bottom fiber (y = −60 mm, tension under sagging moment).
No shear stress, axial force, or transverse loading is considered; only the normal stress σ_x due to bending is required.
All quantities are expressed in a consistent N–mm–MPa unit system.
Present the governing equations clearly, state each assumption explicitly, and report the numerical value of σ_x (in MPa) at each of the three fiber locations.
